newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power weaker amid plentiful hydro.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power weaker amid plentiful hydro.

text.p: Spot power prices in the western U.S. moved slightly lower Thursday, continuing the downtrend begun early in the week amid plentiful hydroelectric supplies, market sources said Thursday.
"It's getting warmer up in the Northwest and there is lots of rain," said one California trader.
He noted power prices were unlikely to rebound from these levels given the increasingly assured abundance of hydroelectric power through next spring.

The National Weather Service recently released an "early bird" forecast for 1997 runoff at The Dalles dam on the Columbia River of 109 percent of historical average levels, compared with 139 percent for 1996.
But industry sources say the 1997 forecast is likely to ratchet upwards when official snowpack measurements begin next month.
Firm, peak electricity at the California-Oregon border (COB) for Friday was quoted at $14.00-16.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), down from lows of $16.00-18.00 for Tuesday through Thursday deals.
Firm, off-peak COB power for Friday was quoted at $9.00-11.00, little changed from the low end of Tuesday through Thursday pre-scheduled prices.
Next-day firm, peak power at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) was pegged at $14.00-$16.00, compared with $15.00-18.00 for Tuesday through Thursday.
Off-peak Mid-C was talked as low as $9.00.
Firm, peak Palo Verde (PV) electricity for Friday was quoted at $14.00-18.00, near the low end of Tuesday through Thursday prices.
Off-peak PV for firm delivery Friday was quoted near $10.00-11.00 per MWh.
Next-day firm, peak prices at Four Corners were in line with PV at around $14.00-17.00. Firm, off-peak Four Corners power was assessed at $12.00-13.00.
